window_order_source_proof.scope: read-only exact-source deduction, no runtime or phone evidence
window_order_source_proof.conclusion: Snapshots preserve current back-to-front stacking order, not creation order. For two ordinary native Wayland windows, activation raises the current window to the final user-app index. Positive horizontal drag means index -1. Once activation snapshot settles, both Foot->Mousepad and Mousepad->Foot therefore require a RIGHT drag. No wrapping exists; LEFT from final index has no target.

source_weakness.status: CONFIRMED source-level counterexample, not reproduced scheduling trace
counterexample: Due service pass advances next_service by33.3ms before processing work. A Flutter platform message makes this pass due and process_events consumes that message, enqueueing a Focus command in runtime wire state.
If elapsed background time reaches2ms at either pre-window-management slice guard, the loop dispatchesZERO and continues before the sole command drain.

On later passes before the next cadence deadline, the queued runtime wire command does not itself make background_services_due true: interactive_service_work_pending only tests pending_shell_actions, pending_shortcut_launches and pending_window_events.
If every due service pass again spends at least2ms before the window-command drain, queued Focus remains indefinitely. No resume cursor/aging guarantee forces this stage to run.
